 Jai Shadlow from Fox Sports 12, Nov • 4m read JackJumpers set for double injury boost as Breakers import closes in on debut - NBL Daily Share The Tasmania JackJumpers could be set for a double injury boost ahead of their road trip, with one import edging closer to a return and another key player preparing to make his season debut.
 Meanwhile, the New Zealand Breakers have received some positive news on an injured import as they look to turn their season around following five consecutive losses.
 All this and more on NBL Daily. 
 JACKJUMPERS SET FOR INJURY BOOST 
 Tasmania JackJumpers import David Johnson has travelled with the team for their Round 9 road trip, raising hopes of a potential return after a calf injury limited him to just eight minutes of action in Round 7.
 JackJumpers assistant coach Mark Radford provided an update on Johnson's availability ahead of their clash against the Perth Wildcats tonight, before the team travels to Brisbane to face the Bullets on Sunday.
 "I think he might be half a chance," Radford said.
 "We've got until Sunday till we play that game. So he's got to still get some work done that's gradually been built up.
 "Obviously, it wasn't as significant as the injury he had last year, so I'll wait and see."
 Prior to his setback, Johnson was playing some of the best basketball of his short NBL career, averaging 16.2 points and 3.1 rebounds while shooting an impressive 56.5% from the field in just 21.1 minutes per game.
 "I would love to have DJ available three weeks ago. He's been unbelievable this year," Radford said.
 "and the thing about him is he's got so much growth. He's really focused on improving his defence so he doesn't get in foul trouble,
 "so he's had a good focus through this period. I can't wait for him to get back."
 Johnson joins a growing injury list for the JackJumpers, which includes Majok Deng (lower leg), Ben Gold (heel), Nick Marshall (ankle) and Bryce Hamilton (ACL), who is also nearing a return after suffering a season-ending injury last season.
 However, Tasmania will receive a boost with the return of guard Ben Ayre, who is preparing to make his season debut after recovering from a hip flexor injury.
 Ayre played 29 games last season, averaging 6.3 points off the bench while providing defensive pressure and energy for Scott Roth's side.
 Now, nearly 10 months since his last appearance, the 30-year-old is set to return to the court, with Radford highlighting the work he has put in during his recovery and the versatility he brings to the roster.
 "I think we'll see a very different Ben Ayre in some aspects of the game that he's been working on off the floor without a doubt," he said.
 "So I'm excited to have him back out there. I love the way he plays and what he brings to our group. And that'll go back to just being able to limit minutes in a couple of other areas because he can play across a couple of positions with his skill set.
 "So great to have him back out there."
 'They know who they are': Blame game erupts over 'selfish' stars in worrying NBL decline 
 The JackJumpers will face the Perth Wildcats at RAC Arena tonight, with tip-off scheduled for 9:30pm AEDT, before travelling to Brisbane for Sunday's clash against the Bullets.
 BREAKERS IMPORT CLOSING IN ON SEASON DEBUT 
 The New Zealand Breakers are currently enduring a five-game losing streak, with injuries continuing to impact their roster, including the loss of MVP-calibre guard Parker Jackson-Cartwright, who was ruled out for the season just days ago.
 However, there is some positive news on the horizon, with import Josiah-Jordan James making progress towards his long-awaited NBL debut.
 In a statement released by the club, the Breakers confirmed James is progressing in his recovery from a hamstring injury, although he is yet to return to full training.
 There is growing hope the American forward could make his first appearance following the FIBA break in December.
 James remains the only import signed during the off-season yet to make his NBL27 debut after suffering the injury during a pre-season clash against Melbourne United, which forced him to leave the game early.
 The 26-year-old from Charleston, South Carolina, arrived in the league with a reputation as a 3&D player, known for his perimeter shooting and defensive ability, which he demonstrated during the NBL Blitz.
 'I should apologise': Hawks coach breaks silence over pointed ref comments as potential NBL sanction looms 
 His eventual return would provide the Breakers with another option at both ends of the floor as they look to overcome their recent struggles.
 While James is still expected to be sidelined for several weeks, New Zealand will be hoping to end their losing streak and build some momentum before the FIBA break, with the forward's return potentially providing a boost heading into December.
